item.title: Gainesville State of the City Address
item.description: Gainesville’s State of the City Address outlines where city leaders say the community is headed each year.But for many residents, the question isn’t what’s being promised – it’s whether those promises match everyday life.Mayor Harvey Ward led the address alongside fellow city commissioners.WUFT’S Andrea Fonseca has more.

item.title: UF students talk about the kindness they encounter
item.description: February 17 marked Random Acts of Kindness Day.

item.title: Another taste of winter, below-freezing temperatures & fire weather for early next week
item.description: Cold temperatures for two nights to start the week, but the coldest night will be Monday night into Tuesday. Strong winds and low humidity levels will increase the wildfire risk across Florida as the extreme drought worsens.

item.title: Q&A: UF's David Kaplan on balancing farming and water quality
item.description: Some water management practices in farming can reduce groundwater pollution and water use while maintaining farm profitability, while others may require financial incentives to be widely adopted, according to a recent UF study.

item.title: Honoring “The Human Fish”: Newton Perry
item.description: In his 79 years of life, Georgia-born Newton Perry, was an underwater cinematographer, the swim coach at Ocala High School, founded Weeki Wachee Springs and opened Perry’s Swim School.

item.title: Columbia County residents spurn project to recharge aquifer
item.description: Columbia County commissioners and residents heard a presentation on Thursday on the Suwannee River Water Management District's project called Water First North Florida.

item.title: Gainesville unplugs at Morningside Nature Center
item.description: The event was meant to get people connected with nature and with the community, according to recreation leader Allison Bordini. It also encouraged visitors to stay off of their phones and be present in nature.

item.title: Photo gallery: Strawberry Festival
item.description: The Bryer Patch, a fourth-generation family-owned produce and flower u-pick at The Boyd Farm in Newberry, held the 4th Annual Strawberry Festival on Saturday.

item.title: Gainesville commission approves over $9.3 million in renovations
item.description: The Gainesville City Commission approved more than $9.3 million in city renovations at a meeting last week. The funding will support projects that will restore historic buildings, improve the city’s emergency operations facilities and renovate community spaces throughout Gainesville.

item.title: Rare breeds and rising stars shine at Galactic Cat Show
item.description: The Galactic Cat Show transformed the Clay County Fairgrounds into a hub for cat lovers this weekend, drawing more than 150 cats from around the world to compete across 10 judging rings.
